clue.text: Private tutor?

blocks.note: surface reading: a tutor who gives one-to-one lessons at home
setter's reading: one who teaches army privates, on the parade ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective for confidential lessons, but it is the noun: a soldier of the lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill sergeant trains new soldiers, the lowest ranks being privates, in marching and parade-ground discipline.

clue.text: Short and funny individual seen on ship

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a short, funny remark

blocks.note: a single individual is one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A brief comic turn is spotted aboard a cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick joke delivered in a single sentence is a brief, witty quip of exactly that kind.

clue.text: Money raised by word of mouth

indicators.note: something passed on by word of mouth is spoken, so we want a word that is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: animals raised on a farm are bred, and the money word is pronounced identically

explanation.surface: Funds are collected by people spreading the word in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is old slang for cash, as dough also is, both being staples one needs to live.

clue.text: An energetic group out to make mischief

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a meddler who is out to make mischief

blocks.note: someone energetic is busy
a body is an organised group, as in a governing body

explanation.surface: A lively band of people set on causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddlesome person who pries into others' affairs often stirs up trouble and gossip as a result.

clue.text: On a winding road it is showing skill

indicators.note: a winding road twists about, so the letters that follow are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver negotiating a twisting road is demonstrating their competence behind the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means deft or dexterous, describing someone who handles things with clever, practised ease.

clue.text: Entrance the prisoner is put out at

indicators.note: the prisoner is stretched or put out to make room, so it spreads around the other word

blocks.note: a prisoner is a captive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A captive is ejected at the doorway of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb pronounced en-TRANCE, to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to put them into a trance-like state of delight, to charm or enthral them.

clue.text: Architectural highlight

blocks.note: surface reading: a building's most striking feature
setter's reading: a source of light set high up, a window projecting from a sloping roof

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' is split into high and light: a window set into the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is an upright window that juts out from a pitched roof, letting daylight into an attic room.

clue.text: Pointless murder weapon?

blocks.note: surface reading: a weapon that serves no purpose
setter's reading: a weapon with no sharp point, like a club or cosh, as detectives say

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' means useless on the surface, but literally it means having no sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Police and pathologists use this phrase for a heavy object without an edge, such as a hammer or club, used to kill.

clue.text: Make a series of calls on zero zero

blocks.note: first meaning: telephone several people in turn
second meaning: zero looks like O, which is a ring, and O is round, so two zeros are a ring and a round

explanation.surface: Someone dials a string of numbers with double zero at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Each zero is the letter O, a ring shape and a round shape, so the pair reads as the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To phone a number of people one after another is a familiar British phrasal verb for canvassing contacts.

clue.text: It forms a ring in two ways

definitions.text: It forms a ring in two ways

blocks.note: first reading: a coral reef that makes a circle around a lagoon
second reading: split after its first letter, it is an article plus the single stroke of a bell, also a ring

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works whole as a ring-shaped reef and split as A TOLL, the sound of a bell ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a circular coral island or reef enclosing a lagoon, typical of tropical oceans.

clue.text: A noted soporific

blocks.note: surface reading: a famous sleeping drug; setter's reading: set to musical notes
something that sends one to sleep, here a song sung to a baby

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' suggests famous, but here it means written in musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a gentle song sung to soothe a child to sleep, so it is a musical sleep-inducer.

clue.text: Seat of Empire

blocks.note: first meaning: a low upholstered stool or footstool
second meaning: belonging to the Turkish empire ruled from Constantinople

explanation.surface: The capital city from which an empire was governed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat of Empire' reads as one phrase, a capital, but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a padded footstool, and the Ottoman Empire was the Turkish state that lasted until 1922.

clue.text: They are naturally charged half portions

indicators.note: only half of the word is wanted, so the front half is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People given only half servings of food are naturally annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests billed or angry, but here it is electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ions are atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge through gaining or losing electrons.

clue.text: Composer to drive men wild

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the preceding letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer whose music drives the men in the audience into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer, a pioneer of opera around 1600.

clue.text: Maybe a place to rest when given the cane badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: a perch is where a bird rests
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolboy given a thrashing might find sitting down uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned or poetic word for perhaps or possibly.

clue.text: Yet its operations donÍt take place here

definitions.text: Yet its operations donÍt take place here

blocks.note: surface reading: a paradox, a place named for operations where none happen
setter's reading: a family doctor's consulting room, where patients are seen but nobody is cut open

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word also means a GP's local practice, where appointments happen but operations are done in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A British general practitioner's premises bear the same name as the medical discipline of operating, hence the paradox.

clue.text: To snub a girl may be wounding

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a sword that may wound

blocks.note: to cut someone is to ignore them deliberately
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Ignoring a young woman can hurt her feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wounding' suggests hurt feelings, but the answer is literally a weapon that wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword favoured by sailors and pirates, a blade that can certainly injure.

clue.text: Papers thrown at union meeting

blocks.note: surface reading: documents hurled in anger at a trade-union gathering
setter's reading: a marriage, where small bits of coloured paper are tossed over the couple

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union meeting' suggests trade unions, but the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are traditionally showered over a bride and groom after the ceremony.

clue.text: Get a role as someoneÍs double

indicators.note: the letters are recast as something else, here a different word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor lands a part as a body double.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is very light here; the acting surface hints that the words are to be recast.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, a person's other identity or close counterpart, Latin for other I.

clue.text: Introduces off cuts

indicators.note: something off is wrong or not right, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone brings in offcuts, the scraps left over from cutting timber or cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off cuts' looks like one word, offcuts, but splits into indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuts in prices, budgets or staff are decreases, the same thing as lowerings or trimmings.

clue.text: Be up in time for a parliamentary occasion

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top
one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: An MP wakes early to attend a sitting of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament hold formal discussions of motions in the chamber, arguing for and against.

clue.text: How one may receive payment of a sort

definitions.text: How one may receive payment of a sort

blocks.note: surface reading: the method of being paid, cash or cheque
setter's reading: paid in goods or services rather than money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of a sort' looks like a vague hedge, but it is the definition: a sort is a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made with goods or favours instead of cash is said to be given this way.

clue.text: Starts to serve time in Russian prison

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A convict begins a sentence in a Siberian jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is long-standing slang for a jail, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Numbers of Romans about the city

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective: relating to a city

blocks.note: C, I, V, I and C are all Roman numerals: 100, 1, 5, 1, 100

explanation.surface: Counting the Roman citizens living around the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the answer is a Roman numeral, so the whole word is a string of Roman numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic describes things belonging to a town or its citizens, such as a civic centre.

clue.text: The standing of a taxi-driver

blocks.note: surface reading: the social status or reputation of a cabbie
setter's reading: the place where taxis stand waiting for fares

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' suggests status, but it is the literal spot where taxis stand in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi stand at a station or street corner is where hired cars queue for passengers.

clue.text: Witty saying has some point with animals

blocks.note: E is east, a point of the compass
two animals, a pig and a ram

explanation.surface: A clever remark makes a point by way of an animal fable.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, pointed and clever remark or poem.

clue.text: Measure associated with Betty Martin

blocks.note: first meaning: the device on an upturned bottle in a British pub that dispenses a fixed tot of spirits
second meaning: to do with the eye, as in the old phrase 'all my eye and Betty Martin', meaning nonsense

explanation.surface: A unit of quantity connected with a woman called Betty Martin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All my eye and Betty Martin' is an old British expression for nonsense, so the eye is linked to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic means relating to the eye, and an Optic is the trademarked spirit dispenser fixed to bottles behind a bar.

clue.text: The opposite of all dressed up and nowhere to go

definitions.text: The opposite of all dressed up and nowhere to go

blocks.clueFragment: all dressed up and nowhere to go
blocks.note: surface reading: the familiar phrase for being ready for a night out with no plans
setter's reading: reverse it, and one is naked with plenty of plans

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works both ways: naked, the opposite of dressed up, and with no engagements, which is like having nowhere to go.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being naked, wearing no clothes whatsoever, which reverses being smartly attired; it also means having no plans.
